title: Digital Forensics Analysts
description: Conduct investigations on computer-based crimes establishing documentary or physical evidence, such as digital media and logs associated with cyber intrusion incidents. Analyze digital evidence and investigate computer security incidents to derive information in support of system and network vulnerability mitigation. Preserve and present computer-related evidence in support of criminal, fraud, counterintelligence, or law enforcement investigations.

tasks.text: Adhere to legal policies and procedures related to handling digital media.
Analyze log files or other digital information to identify the perpetrators of network intrusions.
Perform file signature analysis to verify files on storage media or discover potential hidden files.
Perform forensic investigations of operating or file systems.
Perform web service network traffic analysis or waveform analysis to detect anomalies, such as unusual events or trends.
Conduct predictive or reactive analyses on security measures to support cyber security initiatives.
Create system images or capture network settings from information technology environments to preserve as evidence.
Develop plans for investigating alleged computer crimes, violations, or suspicious activity.
Develop policies or requirements for data collection, processing, or reporting.
Identify or develop reverse-engineering tools to improve system capabilities or detect vulnerabilities.
Maintain knowledge of laws, regulations, policies or other issuances pertaining to digital forensics or information privacy.
Duplicate digital evidence to use for data recovery and analysis procedures.
Maintain cyber defense software or hardware to support responses to cyber incidents.
Preserve and maintain digital forensic evidence for analysis.
Write and execute scripts to automate tasks, such as parsing large data files.
Write cyber defense recommendations, reports, or white papers using research or experience.
Write reports, sign affidavits, or give depositions for legal proceedings.
Write technical summaries to report findings.
Recommend cyber defense software or hardware to support responses to cyber incidents.
Recover data or decrypt seized data.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Amazon Web Services AWS software, Microsoft Access, ServiceNow, Structured query language SQL.

skills.name: Operating system software
skills.def: Software to provide the operational interface to a computer and provide higher-level services and APIs. Examples: Apple iOS, Apple macOS, Bash, Linux.

skills.name: Object or component oriented development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications using object-oriented programming concepts. Examples: C#, C++, Oracle Java, Perl.

skills.name: Development environment software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications which run on a computer or mobile device. Examples: C, Go, Microsoft Azure software, Microsoft PowerShell.

skills.name: Enterprise system management software
skills.def: Software to manage activities across enterprise IT systems, such as evaluating capacity or server availability, monitoring user activities, or installing software. Examples: Splunk Enterprise.

skills.name: Program testing software
skills.def: Software to test or evaluate applications to ensure they comply with specified requirements. Examples: Kali Linux, MITRE ATT&CK software, System testing software.
